newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may extend loan to run-hit Postabank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may extend loan to run-hit Postabank.

text.p: The Hungarian government has authorized Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy to start talks with Postbank owners on the state offering secondary borrowed capital to the run-hit bank, an official said on Thursday.

"The idea came up during the government meeting... where Postabank's Director Gabor Princz informed the government about the bank's situation," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference.
Depositors withdrew around 24 billion forints last month from Postabank, Hungary's second largest commercial bank, in a four-day rumour-triggered panic wave.

Kiss said the government would probably give more details of a possible deal within two weeks, depending on the talks but said there are no details available about the size or maturity of the borrowed capital.
A Postabank official confirmed that Princz was present at the cabinet meeting but did not give further details, only saying the borrowed capital is "basically a long-term loan".
Earlier this month the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) granted Postabank a temporary exemption from the placing of obligatory reserves with the NBH.
Press reports said the exemption is valid until April 15 and frees some 20 billion forints at the bank.
